entry.dc:title: ISCOR UNDERTAKES BOX-CUT TRIAL ON PROMISING COKING COAL PROSPECT.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: In the northern Transvaal on the border of Vendaland, an operation is being carried out by Iscor to determine the viability of exploiting coal deposits by open-cast mining methods. The operation involves a trial box-cut and initial results indicate coal of superior coking quality.

entry.dc:title: On brown coal resources in the Lower Rhine Embayment (West Germany).
entry.dc:creator: Gliese J.
entry.dc:description: The Tertiary brown coal resources in the Lower Rhine Embayment amount to 55,000 million tons. The open-cast mining operations under way or at the planning stage ensure an annual production of 115- 120 million tons over a period fo the next 75 years. The brown coal mainly serves to generate electrical energy. At present about 150-250 m of overburden have to be removed to get at the brown coal. In future, this may increase up to 500 m. The maximum thickness of the brown coal is about 100 m. -from Authors

entry.dc:title: Importance of Lignite for Energy Supplies.
entry.dc:creator: Lenschner
entry.dc:description: Out of 68 Gt of lignite reserves in Western Europe 56 Gt are situated in West Germany, the third largest lignite producer in the world after the USSR and the GDR. In 1977, the output of lignite in West Germany amounted to 123 Mt. 86 TWh of electric power (26% of the total) was produced in West Germany in 1977 by using lignite. The installed capacity of lignite-powered power plants amounts to 14,100 MW. Details about the location of mines and open-cast mining operations are given.

entry.dc:title: ASSESSMENT OF INITIATING SYSTEMS AND THEIR PRACTICAL EFFECT ON BLASTING RESULTS.
entry.dc:creator: Poole G.
entry.dc:description: The merits of various systems for designed initiating columns of explosives in surface mining activities are discussed with special reference to the quarrying and open-cast mining industries, and a comparative analysis of the practical results which can be expected from each system is made. The importance of the safety considerations involved is discussed.

entry.dc:title: LOADER THAT DELIVERS THE GOODS - OR: OPEN CAST MINING AND THE HYDRAULIC EXCAVATOR.
entry.dc:creator: Dos Santos M.
entry.dc:description: The paper discusses the advantages of the hydraulic excavator/loader in open-cast mining.

entry.dc:title: Cable-operated shovels and their prospects in world markets.
entry.dc:creator: Thelen A.
entry.dc:description: The use of cable-operated shovels, excavators, cranes etc. has diminished as a result of the introduction of more efficient, more mobile and hence more economical hydraulically operated equipment. However, there is still a definite niche for cable-controlled equipment, which is still used widely in East European countries and also for particular applications such as transhipment of bulk ores (grab-type cranes), dredging and open-cast mining (e.g. walking draglines). for the ability to reach far from the control cabin (up to 20 m working radius) and for capacity of the bucket which may reach 100 mSUB3 the cable-controlled walking dragline is unsurpassed. (B.D.H.)

entry.dc:title: Damping of boom structure of a rotary excavator by active dynamic vibration attenuators.
entry.dc:creator: Guzhovskiy V.
entry.dc:description: Damping of resonant oscillations of a cantilever structure by an active dynamic vibration attenuator is examined. An optimum valve of the damping coefficient exists which minimises the vibration level in the firsts two natural modes of the structure. The prospects of using active vibration isolators for rotary open-cast mining excavators are discussed. (A)

entry.dc:title: GDR BROWN COAL INDUSTRY - CURRENT OPERATIONS AND FUTURE PLANS.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: Strip-mined brown coal represents a major proportion of East Germany's energy requirements. This article reviews the country's annual production, which totaled 243,468,000 tonnes of brown coal in 1974, open-cast mining machinery and equipment used, and outlines the development of new deposits. East Germany's foreign trade in brown coal is also discussed.

entry.dc:title: WAYS OF IMPROVING THE METHOD OF PRODUCING SHAPED COKE.
entry.dc:creator: Tyutyunnikov Y.
entry.dc:description: New directions of the improvement of the technology of producing shaped coke are considered. The desirability is shown of the separate heating of the components of the charge using noncaking coal as a solid heat carrier. The advantages of the heating of plastic coal moldings by a gaseous heat carrier with the thermal-oxidative pyrolysis of the coking products are described. The social and economic aspects of the problem of producing coke from gas and noncaking coals from open-cast mining are discussed.

entry.dc:title: Lignite: Open-Cast Mining Reaches New Heights.
entry.dc:creator: Tilmann W.
entry.dc:description: Lignite production in the European Community rose from 128. 7 million tons in 1975 to 139. 6 million tons in 1976m, most of it used to supply power plants. The gain in production was made in many coal basins by expanded open-cast mining operations coupled with the opening of new deposits. The author reviews lignite production in the Community by single producing countries, with particular reference to West Germany where lignite accounts for 10% of the total primary energy usage, and where bucket-wheel/belt excavators with 200,000 tons/day capacity are in use.

entry.dc:title: Mine Surveying and Research of Ground Movements in Mines.
entry.dc:creator: Omeltschenko A.
entry.dc:description: This article describes recent work in the mine surveying field that was conducted by East Germany's All-Union Research institute for Rock Mechanics and Mine Surveying. This work included: Orientation of the fixed-point grid underground with the help of a surveying gyroscope; use of new technologies for mine-surveying tasks in open-cast mining; manufacture of new materials for mine-surveying drawings; and new developments in the field of instrument manufacture.

entry.dc:title: AIR POLLUTION AND THE METALLURGICAL INDUSTRY.
entry.dc:creator: Boegman N.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of the South African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: The meteorological conditions in South Africa are not conducive to the effective dispersion of air pollutants. In the light of this, and because of the magnitude, concentration, and future growth potential of the metallurgical industry, control of air pollution is essential. Methods of abatement discussed for each branch of the metallurgical industry, as well as for open-cast mining and bulk ore storage. Some recommendations are made regarding potentially rewarding research and development.

entry.dc:title: LIGNITES OF YUGOSLAVIA IN NATIONAL ECONOMY.
entry.dc:creator: Simonovic M.
entry.dc:description: Lignite accounts for more than four-fifths of Yugoslavia's total fuel reserves. Although the bulk of the country's lignite reserves can be economically worked by open-cast mining methods, the growth of national lignite production has been hindered during the past decade by the availability of cheap, high-quality fuels, chiefly oil. Now, a trend toward the construction of lignite-burning power plants has prompted the accelerated development of this raw material base. The possibility of lignite conversion into higher-grade fuels, primarily synthetic gas, is expected to provide an additional incentive for further future development of lignite.

entry.dc:title: Geological Factors Influencing the Blasting Technique in Open-Cast Mining.
entry.dc:creator: Wild H.
entry.prism:publicationName: Erzmetall Journal for Exploration Mining and Metallurgy
entry.dc:description: The blasting technology is not practicable without the knowledge of the influencing geological factors. While the properties of explosives are well known, the geological factors are not, at least not with regard to blasting techniques. The author attempts to describe the influences of geology and petrography in the blasting methods used in open-cast mining, and lay down rules for carrying out blasting work.

entry.dc:title: NICKEL MINING IN THE DOMINICAN REPUBLIC.
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: One of the Dominican Republic's most important ventures - Falconbridge's lateritic nickel mining and processing operations - is reviewed. The mine and metallurgical complex came onstream at the end of 1971, and during 1974 some 2. 5 million dry short tons of ore were extracted from which 79,643. 6 metric tons ferronickel with 30,492 metric tons contained nickel were produced. The location and geology of the nickel deposit are discussed briefly, and the open-cast mining operation and the metallurgical plant are described in detail.

entry.dc:title: SISHEN ORE RESERVES ESTIMATE UP?
entry.dc:creator: Anon
entry.dc:description: The discovery of iron ore at Sishen was without doubt one of the most exciting developments in South African mining for many years. Many mining men were astounded in 1971 to hear that reserves of iron ore for open-cast mining at Sishen amounted to 1 340 million tonnes. But now with the extensive additional diamond drilling being undertaken in the area it is likely that a much higher estimate of reserves will be made in the very near future. To date a total of over 20 000 metres has been drilled since the 1971 estimate of reserves, and it is expected that recalculations of reserves will be made once the current drilling program is completed.

entry.dc:title: INTRODUCTION OF ANFO BLASTING IN UNDERGROUND MINES.
entry.dc:creator: Bagchi A.
entry.prism:publicationName: Journal of Mines Metals and Fuels
entry.dc:description: The mixture of ammonium nitrate and fuel oil was first used as a blasting agent some 25 years ago. Since then, ANFO, as it is popularly called, has been increasingly used because of its economy and safety as well as efficiency. Thus far, the use of ANFO was confined to open-cast mining, tunneling, excavation work, etc. However, due to the short supply and the spiralling prices of high explosives, the day is not far when ANFO will be used for underground blasting on a large scale in metal mines. In India, the use of ANFO underground has already begun. This paper deals with the trials of ANFO blasting, charging system, hazards involved and their remedy, comparative efficiency and economy, as well as safety factors and other operational practices for better and more efficient utilization of ANFO underground.

entry.dc:title: Recent changes in the conservation value of woodlands in rockingham forest
entry.dc:creator: Peterken G.F.
entry.dc:description: Surveys of all woodlands within Rockingham Forest, Northants, in 1946 and 1972 show that, whilst the total area of woodland remains almost unchanged, considerable changes have taken place in woodland distribution, management systems, crop species, and physiognomy. These changes are quantified and their impact on the value of the woodlands for wildlife conservation and features of interest is assessed by reference to criteria related to the development of the woods. It is concluded that there has been a substantial decline in the conservation value of Rockingham Forest woodlands, caused mainly by State forest policy and open-cast mining, and that this decline is likely to continue. © 1974 Oxford University Press.

entry.dc:title: ELECTRICAL EQUIPMENT FOR THE BELT CONVEYOR SYSTEMS USED IN THE PTOLEMAIS (GREECE) OPEN-CAST MINING OPERATIONS, (ELEKTRISCHE AUSRUESTUNG DER FOERDERBANDANLAGEN IM GRIECHISCHEN TAGEBAU PTOLEMAIS
entry.dc:creator: BOMMER R
entry.dc:description: At this open pit mining site using trains, five bucketwheel excavators and one stacker are supplied with power through a 3km overhead line. Excavators and stackers had to be converted from train to conveyor systems without major hold-ups. The equipment had to be interlocked with the belt conveyor system while follower control gear and safety devices were incorporated. Power supply to the drives was arranged through a central main switch station and kiosk type steel-clad stations.

entry.dc:title: BELT CONVEYOR SYSTEMS USED ON PTOLEMAIS OPEN-PIT MINING SITE, GREECE,
entry.dc:creator: KULLIK E
entry.dc:description: Development of open-cast mining operations, present system and mechanical equipment of the belt conveyor systems of an open-pit mining site converted from combination power shovel, scraper and truck operations to belt conveyor operations. Five bucket-wheel excavators are employed for breaking up and reclaiming materials. In 1969 6 million t of coal were produced, 30% more than originally scheduled. The overburden which varies from sharp-edged rock to sludge and paste presents special difficulties.

entry.dc:title: CRAWLER-MOUNTED THROW- OFF CARRAGES ON OPEN- CAST MINING SITES IN THE CSSR,
entry.dc:creator: DRAZAN F
entry.dc:description: Crawler-mounted dump carriages are used primarily for transfer, tipping, and throw-off operations, supplementing long belt conveyor systems on open-cast mining sites. The paper describes different functions and designs of throw-off carriages and advances typification features. Unit construction is rendered possible by proper selection of types.

entry.dc:title: Forestry on the boulder clay: II. The peterborough meeting, september 1966
entry.dc:creator: Harrison D.
entry.dc:description: Summary: Records briefly the discussion by members at Rockingham on the proper future of these heavy lands and gives some details of the opresent use of 245T-diesel mixtures and Paraquat for the control of vegetation and grasses there. At Hazelborough the meeting was concerned with the silviculture of oak and oak-Norway spruce mixtures. Some description is given of an interesting day spent at Stewart & Lloyd's open-cast mining and restoration work with notes on costs and quality of plantations made on restored ground. The paper comments on some older woods made on mine workings at Boughton and on the woods, including some remarkable Populus robusta, at Elton and ends with an account of the discussion held by the Society on the last evening of the meeting. © 1967 Oxford University Press.
